items.text: Posted about my gym membership renewal last week. Honestly the app itself is fine, but the front desk staff at the Riverside branch seem to have no idea what's going on. I got charged twice for January and had to explain the whole thing three times before anyone fixed it. I even showed them the confirmation email the assistant pulled up for me, and they still looked confused. Has anyone else had billing issues since the new system went live?

items.text:
I've been a Crestline Home customer for six years and I want to flag how the return of my faulty kettle was handled. The support agent was polite, but the refund only landed after three separate chats, and nobody ever sent a confirmation I could keep.

I know these things happen. What bothered me was that each person I spoke to seemed to start from scratch, even though I'd already explained everything and the assistant had summarised the case for me. A little continuity would go a long way.

I'm not asking for anything dramatic, just a proper acknowledgment and perhaps a note on the account so the next person knows where things stand.

items.text: Just got my refund sorted for the ProBook 14 I bought at Northgate Electronics. Took eleven days from the day I shipped it back, which is slower than the two weeks they promised but at least it arrived. The automated tool emailed me a tracking link every couple of days, which helped. Anyone thinking of returning a laptop to them: keep the original box and photograph the serial number before you send it.

items.text: Quick tip for anyone using the PeakForm app to manage their gym membership: the renewal reminder defaults to the day before billing, which is too late to cancel. I changed mine to a week ahead. The bot that answers their chat line had no idea this setting even existed, so I wouldn't bother asking it. Has anyone found a way to export the billing history?

items.text:
Sharing my experience with Brightline Appliances after my blender died two weeks out of warranty. Their phone support was fine, but the return portal kept rejecting my proof of purchase because it wanted a PDF, not a photo. I ended up emailing the picture to a person, who fixed it in about a day.

The actual refund took about ten days, which is typical. I don't have a huge complaint; I just think their portal could be clearer about file formats. If you're in the same boat, call them rather than fighting the automated system for a week.
